answer: For a garden-monitoring network, require each paid archive to store an identity-bound, incompressible replica. Publish its commitment as an anchor before random audits are drawn. Each audit demands a fresh nonce-bound proof, so an old echo cannot be replayed. Use overlapping short deadlines and slow replica encoding: aliases sharing one disk cannot claim extra bytes without new storage or costly recomputation. Pay for proven capacity, never the number of identities.
